doc.title: ZNY–ZDC LOA
doc.summary: Interfacility LOA between vZNY and vZDC: MIT, separation, coordination, transfer-of-control rules and closed-facility procedures, plus route/altitude tables for traffic in both directions (incorporating PCT, N90, ACY and DOV restrictions).

items.title: Purpose, scope, disclaimer, cancellation
items.text: Prescribes airspace delegation, operational procedures and coordination between vZNY and vZDC; applies to all ZDC and ZNY controllers and facilities and incorporates PCT and N90 coordination and routing restrictions. VATSIM use only. Cancels the ZNY & ZDC LOA dated 23 April 2015 and incorporates the New York ARTCC & Atlantic City TRACON and Philadelphia TRACON & Dover RAPCON LOAs (both dated 23 April 2015).

items.title: Centers assume unstaffed TRACON airspace
items.text: Washington and New York Centers shall assume control of TRACON airspace within their respective ARTCCs if the TRACON position is not manned. When this occurs, all airspace and altitude restrictions apply.

items.title: Early service before entering other facility
items.text: ZNY or ZDC may provide enroute service to aircraft before they enter the other facility's airspace when the other facility is not open. Upon opening, aircraft already receiving service may remain with the controlling facility, which uses an automated point out to show the aircraft is on its frequency; if the opening facility needs control it coordinates a handoff.

items.title: Separation minima
items.text: Minimum lateral separation is 5nm constant or increasing, except aircraft FL230 and below may be laterally separated by 3nm if separation is increasing to 5nm.

items.title: Kennedy area arrivals: 10 MIT
items.text: ZDC will provide ZNY 10 MIT minimum for Kennedy Area arrivals on the same or geographically similar route. (Kennedy Area satellites are not defined in this LOA.)

items.title: LaGuardia area arrivals: 10 MIT
items.text: ZDC will provide ZNY 10 MIT minimum for LaGuardia Area arrivals on the same or geographically similar route.

items.title: Newark area arrivals: 10 MIT
items.text: ZDC will provide ZNY 10 MIT minimum for Newark Area arrivals on the same or geographically similar route.

items.title: Philadelphia area arrivals: 10 MIT on JIIMS
items.text: ZDC will provide ZNY 10 MIT on the JIIMS STAR for Philadelphia Area arrivals. ZDC will sequence IROKT and HEKMN as one.

items.title: Same route/same altitude: 5 miles
items.text: Aircraft on the same route segment and at the same altitude shall be separated by no less than 5 miles, and increasing, regardless of cruise altitude. Aircraft destined to the same airport need not have in-trail spacing applied if altitude separated unless otherwise required by this agreement or active traffic management initiatives are in effect.

items.title: Altitude for direction of flight before handoff
items.text: Unless otherwise required or coordinated by this agreement, aircraft must be climbing to, descending to, or level at the correct altitude for direction of flight prior to any handoff.

items.title: Dover AFB and satellite departures into PHL
items.text: Departures from DOV RAPCON entering PHL TRACON will be cleared on course at or below 7000, appropriate altitude for direction of flight. Controllers ensure any necessary coordination is accomplished. (DOV satellites are not defined in this LOA.)

items.title: ACY departures entering ZNY: climb to 7000
items.text: Atlantic City TRACON departures entering ZNY will be climbed to 7000 and cleared on course.

items.title: ACY-area traffic landing JFK: routing
items.text: Aircraft landing JFK or JFK satellites will be routed via ACY V184 PANZE V44 CAMRN.

items.title: ACY arrivals from ZNY: direct KACY, 8000
items.text: Arrivals to ACY may be cleared by ZNY direct to KACY without prior coordination and will be assigned 8000 prior to communications transfer. ACY has control for descent on contact and turns of 30 degrees left or right of course south of the CYN R-100.

items.title: Automated point outs
items.text: Automated point outs without further verbal/textual coordination are authorized when the datablock accurately reflects the aircraft's current clearance. If an interim altitude is entered, approval of the point out releases control for climb or descent to the flight plan altitude, or the top or bottom of the approving sector's stratum.

items.title: Consolidation / deconsolidation
items.text: Before consolidating or deconsolidating (or opening or closing) any position that shares a mutual boundary, coordinate with all affected controllers in the neighboring ARTCC. General ATC chat or private chat is acceptable.

items.title: Holding at arrival fixes
items.text: When holding is required at arrival fixes, ZDC or ZNY retain communications and control of holding patterns within their delegated airspace. During airborne holding, both hold at published holding fixes unless coordinated otherwise.

items.title: Routing: PRD, LOA supersedes
items.text: The FAA Preferred Route Database (PRD) should be used for all originating and terminating aircraft in ZNY or ZDC. If routing requirements in this agreement differ from the PRD, the LOA routing supersedes the PRD.

items.title: Handoffs: conflicts resolved, datablock accurate
items.text: Automated handoffs are initiated only after all conflicts are resolved and no further control instructions will be given. The datablock and flight plan must reflect the clearance; route amendments (QU or AM) must be made whenever a route clearance is amended (e.g. "CLEARED DIRECT <FIX>").

items.title: Climbing aircraft: highest interim altitude, QQ
items.text: Aircraft climbing to a requested cruise altitude not yet cleared to it are climbed to the highest interim altitude available based on traffic, airspace or LOA requirements. "QQ" is used for the assigned altitude and constitutes a coordinated altitude when an automated handoff is used.

items.title: Descending aircraft: update QZ
items.text: Aircraft descending to a new assigned altitude have their flight plan altitude (QZ) updated. Interim altitudes for descending aircraft should generally not be used unless the pilot-requested lower altitude is not available and the interim altitude is the lowest available with that controller.

items.title: ERAM fourth line entries
items.text: ERAM fourth line entries made in accordance with FAAO 7110.65 are authorized for coordination. The receiving controller should not accept a handoff and should initiate coordination if there is any doubt about a fourth line entry's meaning.

items.title: Transfer at Attachment 1/2 altitudes
items.text: Aircraft enroute between centers must be transferred at the altitudes/flight levels specified in Attachments 1 and 2 unless otherwise coordinated.

items.title: No re-route required if OK to first fix
items.text: One center must not require the other to change or issue routing if the routing is satisfactory to the first route fix in the receiving center's area.

items.title: ZNY turns 20 deg north of V268 (J220/Q221/Q227/HGR)
items.text: ZNY shall have control for turns 20 degrees or less, north of V268, for traffic routed J220/Q221/Q227 or Hagerstown VOR.
items.restr: ZNY turns <=20 deg N of V268

items.title: ZNY turns 20 deg north of Woodstown (Q22)
items.text: ZNY shall have control for turns 20 degrees left or right of course north of Woodstown VORTAC for traffic routed Q22.
items.restr: ZNY turns 20 deg N of OOD

items.title: ZNY may clear Q437/Q409 direct VILLS
items.text: ZNY may clear traffic routed via Q437/Q409 direct VILLS without prior coordination.

items.title: ZDC may clear Q22-and-west traffic direct JFK
items.text: ZDC may clear traffic routed via Q22 or west direct JFK without prior coordination.

items.title: 15 deg turns within 15nm of boundary
items.text: Unless otherwise specified, ZDC and ZNY each have control for turns up to 15 degrees within 15 miles of the common boundary for aircraft in level flight, and for climbing/descending aircraft if the turn is accomplished within the transferring controller's stratum.

items.title: Turbojets NE-bound on Q22 AOA FL230
items.text: Turbojet traffic northeast bound on Q22 shall be at or above FL230.

items.title: No Q221 for DC-area departures to SWF
items.text: ZDC will not route aircraft destined to SWF and SWF area airports departing the Washington metro area via Q221.

items.title: ZNY closed: ZDC hands off direct to N90/PHL
items.text: When ZNY is closed, ZDC may hand off directly to any N90 position that would otherwise have received a handoff from ZNY, assigning the lowest usable flight level based on the ACY altimeter; N90 has control for turn and descent. N90 and PHL may hand off departures via J6/J48/Q75, DIXIE or WHITE to ZDC at the top altitude that would have been assigned for a handoff to ZNY; ZDC has control for turn and climb.

items.title: ZDC closed: ZNY hands off direct to PCT
items.text: When ZDC is closed, ZNY may hand off directly to any PCT position that would otherwise have received a handoff from ZDC or another PCT area. Aircraft may be given a descend via clearance or 10,000 as appropriate. PCT may hand off departures leaving the PCT terminal area to the north or east to ZNY at the appropriate top altitude; ZNY has control for turn and climb.
